analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: Any FOMC rate hike doubts put to bed by CPI & Waller
key_insights: The 2-year UST yield rose nearly 20bp on 10 Nov, the biggest one-day jump since April 2024 (Liberation Day) and, before that, October 2024. A stronger than expected CPI print followed hawkish comments from Fed Governor Waller.
The OIS market is partially pricing a 50bp hike at the 9 December FOMC. MUFG says this is driven more by Waller's comments than by the CPI print itself.
Waller argued that sticky inflation and energy risks warrant reversing the 75bp of cuts, and asked why wait two meetings to do it. Fed President Logan also called for more rapid rate increases.

MUFG assumes Waller did not know the CPI data when he spoke in London 4.5 hours before the release. OMB statistical policy limits advance knowledge to a small number of designated officials at the producing agency.
MUFG is sceptical of a 50bp hike and expects most FOMC members to prefer 25bp. A 50bp hike is a risk, not the core view.

A scenario for a more aggressive December hike is a strong payrolls report plus a rebound in crude oil after the recent sharp drop. That would give President Trump more reason to seek a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
A more hawkish Fed outcome would shift rate expectations in favour of the dollar. MUFG says it would likely push EUR/USD lower and bring levels below 1.1000 into play.
USD/JPY is back near 160, above which MUFG says intervention becomes much more likely. JGBs sold off in line with Treasuries, with little curve steepening (2s10s 2bps steeper, 2s30s flat).
A JGB auction on 10 Nov had a bid-to-cover of 3.36, slightly weaker than the 12-month average. The FT reported strong demand for JGBs from Japanese households.
MoF data shows JGB issuance to individuals (3, 5 and 10-year) at JPY 2,026bn for November, the largest single month. August was a record JPY 1,108bn, followed by another record in September.

45% of Japanese households' USD 16trn of assets (USD 7.1trn) sits in cash deposits. The BoJ has formally confirmed the 2% inflation goal, and speculation is growing that JGB holdings may be added to tax-free NISA accounts or exempted from inheritance tax.
MUFG sees risks skewed toward yen strength over the medium term, as intervention caps upside in USD/JPY and confidence in the BoJ improves.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The print came after Waller's hawkish comments and triggered the largest 2-year yield jump since April 2024.
Markets are reconsidering the Fed's path, with partial pricing of a 50bp hike.

macro_indicators.indicator: OIS pricing of Fed hike at 9 December FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: A larger hike is a tail risk. MUFG's base case is 25bp.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed cuts to reverse per Waller
macro_indicators.interpretation: Waller argues for reversing the cuts quickly rather than waiting two meetings.
Would come into play if rate hike expectations shift further in the dollar's favour.
Above this level intervention becomes a much greater prospect.
Slightly weaker than the 12-month average, though overall JGB sentiment has improved.
Largest single-month total, signalling a possible gradual shift in Japanese household flows toward domestic assets.

risk_factors: A strong payrolls print combined with a crude oil rebound could push the Fed toward a 50bp hike in December.
The debate over whether Waller knew the CPI data in advance could affect confidence in Fed communication.
A further hawkish Fed repricing could push EUR/USD below 1.1000.

Chart of issuance of JGBs to individuals in Japan (source: Ministry of Finance Japan and MUFG Research).
vol_and_positioning: USD/JPY near 160 marks the level above which intervention becomes a much greater prospect.
The OIS market is partially pricing a 50bp Fed hike on 9 December, a sharp change from before the CPI print and Waller's comments.
geopolitical: Trade-off between oil prices and the Iran conflict: a rebound in crude could add to the reasons for President Trump to push for a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the conflict.
Political fallout and potential AI consequences of the US mid-term election results had been the market's focus before the CPI print.

tension_points.bull_case: The dollar bull case is that Waller and Logan push for faster hikes, sticky inflation and energy risks persist, and OIS pricing moves toward a 50bp hike, which would lift the dollar and push EUR/USD below 1.1000.
tension_points.bear_case: MUFG is sceptical of the need for 50bp and expects most FOMC members to see better risk-reward in 25bp. A 50bp hike remains more a risk than a core view.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak payrolls report, or crude oil staying lower after its recent sharp drop, would weigh against a 50bp hike. A strong payrolls print plus a crude rebound would support it.

tension_points.bull_case: The yen could strengthen as JGB demand from Japanese households picks up, BoJ confidence improves, and intervention limits USD/JPY upside.
tension_points.bear_case: The yen weakened sharply after the US CPI data, and USD/JPY is back near 160 as US yields rise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further sharp US yield rises that push USD/JPY past 160 without intervention would weaken the yen-strength case.

theme_stances.key_argument: MUFG doubts a 50bp hike is needed and expects most FOMC members to prefer 25bp.
theme_stances.evidence: We remain sceptical of the need to hike by 50bps at this stage

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising household JGB demand and improved BoJ confidence, with intervention capping upside, skew risks toward yen strength.
theme_stances.evidence: the risks certainly look more skewed to yen strength over the medium term
